supporting_observations.claim: WS-TWEBER-01 made repeated HTTPS CONNECT requests to update.medledger.co:443 at roughly five-minute intervals from 13:41:49 through 14:11:26 UTC. One attempt at 13:46:52 was denied; the other cited attempts were allowed as tunnels.

Endpoint telemetry associates these proxy connections with medledgerupd.exe running from Tom Weber's user-profile AppData directory, rather than the approved inventory path under C:\Program Files\MediLedger.

The observed hostname, update.medledger.co, differs from the approved MediLedger update hostname, update.medledger.com. Combined with the executable's non-inventory path, this makes the activity suspicious, but does not establish that the domain or executable is malicious.

The repeated requests have similar proxy-reported byte counts and durations, and the executable exited at 14:11:35; these facts are consistent with recurring updater checks but do not verify the connection content or software legitimacy.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT tunnels to port 443, not the HTTPS request paths or payloads; the cited records do not provide TLS certificate details or establish what content was exchanged.
The evidence shows the process path and network association, but does not provide the executable's hash, signature status, installation provenance, or comparison with a known-good MediLedger updater.
The supplied records do not establish whether update.medledger.co is controlled by MediLedger, a typo, or a malicious lookalike.
claims_not_established: That the executable is authentic, tampered with, or malicious.
That update.medledger.co is legitimate or malicious, or that it is controlled by MediLedger.
That the HTTPS exchanges delivered or executed an update, or carried harmful content.
That the periodic connections caused compromise or data exfiltration.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve the executable and collect its hash, signature and certificate status, file metadata, creation and download provenance, and comparison with a known-good MediLedger package.
Validate ownership and reputation of update.medledger.co and compare its DNS, TLS certificate, and infrastructure with the approved update.medledger.com service.
Collect fuller proxy and endpoint network telemetry, including available TLS metadata and any application logs, to determine what the tunnels exchanged.
Check whether the AppData installation and this hostname are expected for this workstation's MediLedger deployment.
unrelated_findings: WS-ESTONE-01 and WS-ARUIZ-01 made TLS connections to WS-TWEBER-01 on port 443, with the server name WS-TWEBER-01.pinecrest.local.
